evidence: run c5t22_s124942050: first unmapped point entered <1 m at t=3.23 s (bearing -67°) but collision occurred at t=7.38 s with mover ahead (partner_rel_xy [0.24, -0.52])
run c5t22_s1843695807: mover behind detected only at t=52.23 s (2 m away) and collision at t=54.83 s (partner_rel_xy [-0.39, -0.53]) – rear backup never triggered (x>-0.5)
all three runs use the same controller logic (VO, predictive speed, rear backup) yet collisions happen despite mover being visible in raw lidar <2 s before impact

assumptions.assumption: Clustering‑tracking reliably detects a mover before it is <1 m from the robot
assumptions.why: First_not_on_map shows unmapped points <1 m appear 2–3 s before collision, but M is still empty or inaccurate

assumptions.assumption: VO planner can find a safe (v,w) when any mover is inside _SAFE_DIST (3 m)
assumptions.why: Collisions occur while VO is active; the planner either returns None or a command that still leads to impact

assumptions.assumption: Rear‑backup suffices for collisions caused by objects behind the robot
assumptions.why: Two collisions involve objects in front/right; rear backup never activates

assumptions.assumption: Predictive speed scaling based on tracked movers prevents high‑speed impacts
assumptions.why: When tracking works, speed is reduced; however failures happen when tracking is delayed

assumptions.assumption: Lidar‑strip and swept‑body checks in _guard catch all imminent contacts
assumptions.why: Movers not yet tracked appear in raw points and can breach the robot body before _guard sees them

approach_families.family: predictive speed / dynamic pause (based on tracked TTC)
approach_families.result: 4/5 passes in turn 2, but later attempts fell back to collisions
mixed; best 7/10 passes in turn 17, still several front‑collision failures
4/7 passes – still some collisions when stop not followed by safe retreat

candidates.idea: Hybrid raw‑point TTC stop + predictive speed: call _raw_ttc_stop right after perception, enforce a pause when TTC<0.8 s, then resume using existing _predictive_speed logic
candidates.for: detects imminent front collisions before tracking can identify the mover
candidates.risk: may cause frequent short stops on noisy points, reducing overall throughput

candidates.idea: Full‑direction backup using raw unmapped points: when any point is within 0.8 m of the robot body, compute a reverse command with _px_backup_cmd (front or side) and execute it for 0.5 s, independent of tracking
candidates.for: reacts to close obstacles from any direction, not only behind
candidates.risk: backup could drive into another obstacle or wall if guard checks miss a fast‑moving object

candidates.idea: Increase VO horizon to 4 s and tighten VO‑fail timeout to 0.3 s, forcing a quicker fallback to side‑detour when VO cannot find a safe command
candidates.for: gives VO more look‑ahead while reducing time spent in an unsafe dead‑end
candidates.risk: longer horizon may be too conservative, causing unnecessary detours or stalls

diagnosis.chosen: Candidate 1 (Hybrid raw‑point TTC stop + predictive speed) is selected because it directly addresses the observed delay between raw point appearance and tracking, and it re‑uses the already‑tested predictive‑speed module to resume motion safely.
diagnosis.target: controller (insert early TTC stop logic and pause handling)
diagnosis.direction: 1. After _perceive(st, t, pose) add a call: pause = _raw_ttc_stop(st, t, pose). 2. If pause is not None, set st['pause_until'] = max(st.get('pause_until', -1.0), t + pause) and return (0.0, 0.0, False). 3. When t >= st['pause_until'], clear st['vo_until'] and st['detour'] to avoid stale commands. 4. Keep the existing predictive‑speed call for normal motion (vc = _predictive_speed(...)). 5. Adjust _raw_ttc_stop thresholds (TTC_THRESHOLD = 0.8 s, distance limit = 1.5 m) to be more aggressive. 6. All commands still pass through _guard for final swept‑body and lidar‑strip safety.
